profile.campus_mw_context: The 128,715-sq. ft. data center in Sterling, VA, offers 11 MW of IT capacity and features robust connectivity options with high bandwidth and high-availability circuits and a number of metro and long-haul networks.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA4 in Sterling offers 11 MW of IT capacity across 128,715 square feet, equivalent to roughly 275 racks at typical AI training density. The facility emphasizes network connectivity with multiple metro and long-haul circuits, addressing data movement constraints for distributed workloads rather than power density.

Virginia hosts 330 mapped data centers, but only 25 publish capacity figures. This facility ranks 26th among those with disclosed capacity, representing less than 1% of Virginia's publicly documented total of 1,603 MW. The gap between mapped and disclosed capacity means Virginia's true aggregate power remains largely hidden.

The facility's 11 MW positions it for enterprise workloads, specialized compute, or distributed inference where connectivity quality matters more than raw power. It is unlikely to support frontier model training runs. Whether modest facilities like this matter to AI scaling depends on whether the 305 unmapped or unpublished facilities in Virginia contain larger campuses nearby, and whether published capacity figures undercount the state's actual infrastructure.
